item.text: {"question_id":"3B.10","answer":"The supplied evidence does not establish that people were durably safer from state and non-state violence than under the inherited baseline by the end of 2023. Direct period-end evidence instead documents severe, recurring state-attributed physical-integrity and detention abuses: crimes-against-humanity findings, mass arbitrary detention, torture, enforced disappearance, long imprisonment of minorities, and lack of credible punishment for abusive officials (BATCH-0001-E005; BATCH-0001-E006; BATCH-0010-E024; BATCH-0022-E012). Political prosecutions, suppression of journalism and dissent, and the absence of an official investigation into alleged lockdown abuses further weaken evidence of effective remedy or restrained crisis governance (BATCH-0020-E007; BATCH-0020-E008; BATCH-0022-E015). Xi’s public characterization of Xinjiang policy as a success supplies direct ruler-period endorsement of the relevant policy direction, although the country-level evidence does not attribute every individual abuse to a personal order (BATCH-0010-E024). There is some qualifying evidence of institutional or administrative capacity: 2023 healthcare coverage and medical assistance, education spending, social-assistance coverage, and a trafficking prosecution indicate material provision or a remedy in selected cases, but these are indirect or limited safety evidence and do not demonstrate reduced exposure to state or non-state violence, prevention, equitable protection, or durable improvement (BATCH-0016-E009; BATCH-0013-E006; BATCH-0026-E012; BATCH-0026-E018). A 2023 security speech records proposals for counterterrorism and regional security cooperation, not domestic implementation or outcomes (BATCH-0023-E016). Earlier legal safeguards against torture-derived evidence and required interrogation recording are inherited institutional conditions, not evidence of 2023 compliance or Xi-specific improvement; research also finds continuing party-state dependence of courts and weak defense protections (BATCH-0027-R01-E001; BATCH-0008-E010; BATCH-0008-E011). The closed information environment, including severe press restrictions and regional information controls, makes low reported violence or silence non-probative (BATCH-0020-E008; BATCH-0022-E012). External shocks and the lack of comparable exposure-adjusted violence data further limit causal attribution. Severity is best classified as systematic repression with documented crimes-against-humanity findings in Xinjiang, rather than a claim that the supplied record establishes nationwide mass-terror
